Measured positive, reinforced by easier business credit but tempered by pockets of consumer and CRE caution. The FOMC statement highlights strong labor markets, inflation drifting toward 2 percent, and a gradual, still-accommodative policy path. The January 2018 SLOOS adds that banks eased standards and terms for C&I loans (including narrower loan rate spreads and easier credit line terms), citing competition, a better economic outlook, higher risk tolerance, and secondary market liquidity; banks also expect to ease standards for small firms and narrow spreads further, with some expecting improved quality for nonsyndicated loans. Offsetting this, SLOOS shows tighter standards and weaker demand in CRE—especially construction and land development—and mixed-to-tighter conditions in consumer credit (credit cards/HELOCs), with some banks expecting performance to deteriorate. Taken together, credit supply to businesses is supportive of growth, while consumer and CRE segments counsel caution, consistent with the Financial Stability Report’s valuation/leverage concerns and the FOMC’s gradualism.
